prompts: Words are tied to each other, and nobody here can see how. {WS}/site is a saved copy of a Portuguese creative dictionary. Explore this universe of words: collect what the site knows and build {WS}/universe/index.html, a single file that sums the universe up in one view and lets someone search for a word and find how it relates to others. The best way to show it is your call, and that view is what we care about most. So people can share a word, opening the page with ?word=saudade must show that word and its relations. Save the data as {WS}/words.json, mapping each word to the words it is linked to, and record in {WS}/result.json: words (how many), relations (how many distinct pairs) and most_connected. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal] Map the word links in `./site` and build a one-view page with search and `?word=` sharing.

[action]
- Parsed the 250 word pages, using only the Sinônimos and Palavras análogas sections as relations. I ignored the "Palavras do dia", "Destaques" and "Mais buscadas" lists because they are site-wide navigation, not word links.
- Followed the meta-refresh redirect pages (`paixoes`, `saudades`, `coracoes`) to their real target, so `saudades` counts as `saudade`.
- Matched hrefs to files ignoring case and percent-encoding, and named each word from its page `<h1>`, lowercased.
- Counted each relation as an undirected pair, once, with no self-links.
- Skipped 7 links to pages that don't exist (`rascunho-3`, `em-construcao`, `link-antigo`, `pagina-removida`, `xpto-2`).
- Wrote `words.json`, `result.json` and `universe/index.html`.
- The page is one self-contained file with the data embedded. It draws a force-directed canvas graph. Node colour is the page's "Tema" (10 themes, with a legend) and node size is the number of links. It uses no CDN, so three.js is not needed.
- Search has autocomplete. `?word=saudade` centres that word, highlights its links and lists them, and clicking any word updates the URL. You can drag nodes, pan and zoom. An unknown word shows a "not in this dictionary" message.

[result]
- `result.json` content: `{"words": 250, "relations": 743, "most_connected": "tempo"}`.
- `palavra` and `tempo` tie at 16 links each. I picked `tempo` by alphabetical order, which is my assumption.
- The 250 pages gave 250 distinct names, so no two pages merge into one word.
- `node --check` passes on the page script. I did not open the page in a browser, so the rendering and the `?word=` behaviour are untested.

[next] Open `universe/index.html?word=saudade` in a browser to confirm the view.
